finding.title: POST /api/payment/request has no order-status guard — a payment link can be minted for an already-paid/cancelled order
finding.suggested_fix: Only allow payment initiation when order.status === 'pending_payment' (return 400 otherwise) before calling paymentRouter.requestPaymentWithFailover and before overwriting `authority`.

finding.title: markOrderPaid double-credits VIP points under concurrent verify callbacks on PostgreSQL
finding.suggested_fix: On PG (READ COMMITTED) two concurrent /verify callbacks can both read status='pending_payment' and both credit points. Make the transition atomic: UPDATE orders SET status='processing' WHERE id=? AND status='pending_payment' RETURNING, and only credit points when a row was returned (same pattern as the oversell fix in orders.ts).

finding.title: User cancel: check-then-act status guard is not atomic — concurrent double-cancel double-restocks and double-refunds on PG
finding.suggested_fix: Perform the status flip first with an atomic predicate: UPDATE orders SET status='cancelled' WHERE id=? AND status IN ('pending_payment','processing') RETURNING; if no row, abort. Then restock/refund once. Same defect exists in the cancel branch of PUT /api/admin/orders/:id/status (admin.ts:526-550).

finding.title: Coupon usage cap is TOCTOU on PostgreSQL — concurrent orders can exceed usageLimit
finding.suggested_fix: Apply the same atomic-predicate pattern used for stock: UPDATE coupons SET used_count = used_count + 1 WHERE code = ? AND (usage_limit IS NULL OR used_count < usage_limit) RETURNING code; if 0 rows, reject the coupon. The read-only check at line 154 is racy on PG.

finding.title: Address CRUD functions close over stale `user` state — concurrent/repeated address mutations lose data
finding.evidence: const addAddress = async (address) => { if (!user) return; ... setUser({ ...user, addresses: [...(user.addresses || []), data.address] }); } — same pattern in updateAddress (setUser({...user, addresses: user.addresses.map(...)})), deleteAddress and setDefaultAddress. All four spread the `user` captured at render time instead of using functional updates.
finding.suggested_fix: Use functional updates: setUser(prev => prev ? { ...prev, addresses: [...] } : null) in all four address functions, so consecutive awaits (e.g. addAddress then setDefaultAddress) don't overwrite each other's result.

finding.title: Guest-cart merge can silently drop guest items if a push fails, and is not aborted on logout
finding.evidence: const pushGuest = guestItems.map(item => authFetch('/api/cart', {...}).catch(err => console.error('Failed to merge guest cart item', err))); Promise.all(pushGuest).then(() => authFetch('/api/cart', ...)).then(data => { if (Array.isArray(data)) { setCart(data); localStorage.setItem('cart', JSON.stringify(data)); } }) — a failed POST is swallowed, then the authoritative server list unconditionally REPLACES local state, destroying the guest item.
finding.suggested_fix: Fail the merge (keep local state) when any push rejects, e.g. throw inside the catch so Promise.all rejects and the replace is skipped; or re-push failed items.

finding.title: Header login modal has no role="dialog", no aria-modal, no focus trap, no Escape close
finding.evidence: <div className="fixed inset-0 z-[9999] flex items-center justify-center p-4 sm:p-6 overflow-y-auto"> — no role/aria-modal attributes anywhere in the file (grep shows only body-overflow effects at lines 29-41); focus is never moved into the modal nor trapped, so keyboard/SR users can tab into background content and Escape does not close it.
finding.suggested_fix: Add role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label, autofocus the first field, trap Tab within the panel, close on Escape (CartDrawer.tsx and Blog.tsx already do this).

finding.title: Refresh token accepted from JSON body, and both tokens returned in JSON response — HttpOnly cookie protection undermined
finding.suggested_fix: Remove the `req.body.refreshToken` fallback and stop spreading `...tokens` into JSON responses (register/login/otp/verify/refresh all do this). Rely solely on the HttpOnly cookies; the client already uses cookie-based refresh via authFetch. Keeping tokens out of JS-readable responses makes XSS token exfiltration materially harder.

finding.title: No refresh-token rotation state or revocation: logout/compromise cannot invalidate a live refresh token (7d TTL)
finding.suggested_fix: Rotation reissues a fresh pair (good) but old refresh tokens stay valid until 7d expiry — /logout only clears cookies server-side and there is no token-version/jti denylist. Add a `tokenVersion` (or jti) column on users, embed it in the refresh JWT, check+increment on logout/password change/admin password reset (server/routes/admin.ts:289 sets a new password but any stolen refresh token still works).

finding.title: 12 admin mutation endpoints have no Zod validate() middleware (hand-rolled, inconsistent checks)
finding.evidence:
router.put('/users/:id/password', async (req, res) => { const { newPassword } = req.body; if (!newPassword || typeof newPassword !== 'string' || newPassword.length < 6) {...}
// also unvalidated: /users/:id/role (317), /users/:id/points (344), /products (372), /products/:id (404), /orders/:id/status (511), /coupons (593), /coupons/:code (635), /orders/:id/tracking (803), /reviews/:id/approved (841), /contact-messages/:id/status (717), /settings (935)
finding.suggested_fix: Add Zod schemas in server/validators (adminPasswordSchema, roleSchema, pointsSchema, productUpsertSchema, orderStatusSchema, couponUpsertSchema, trackingSchema, approvedSchema, messageStatusSchema, settingsSchema) and pass to validate() like cart/orders/auth routes already do. Admin-only status lowers exploitability but parseInt()-coercion gaps (e.g. `parseInt(stockQuantity) || 0` silently zeroes stock on garbage input) are real logic bugs.

finding.title: Stock/price changes never bust the `product:<id>` detail cache — invalidate('products') does not match 'product:<id>' keys
finding.suggested_fix: 'products' is not a substring of 'product:5', so GET /api/products/:id keeps serving stale stockQuantity/price for up to 60s after an order, cancellation, or admin product edit. Invalidate('product:') (prefix) or call appCache.invalidate() with no pattern for product mutations.

finding.title: PUT /api/cart/:id accepts any quantity — max-10 and stock guards are not enforced on update
finding.suggested_fix: Validate 1 <= quantity <= 10 and quantity <= product.stockQuantity (as POST / does). Currently a client can set quantity=999999; the invariant is only rescued later by the order-transaction stock guard.

finding.title: VIP clawback can drive vipPoints negative
finding.suggested_fix: If an admin adjusted the user's points (PUT /api/admin/users/:id/points sets an absolute value) after the order was credited, the clawback subtracts from a balance that may not contain those points, producing a negative vip_points. Clamp with SQL: set vipPoints = MAX(0, vipPoints - X) or guard with vipPoints >= X.

finding.title: PUT /api/users/me can take an already-registered phone — unique-constraint violation surfaces as a generic 500
finding.suggested_fix: Pre-check `phone` uniqueness (or catch the constraint error and return 400 with a Persian message). A failed unique index currently yields a generic 500 and the profile update is silently lost.

finding.title: User-visible cart-limit toasts render English digits (۹۹ shown as 99)
finding.evidence: addToast(`حداکثر تعداد مجاز (${MAX_CART_QUANTITY} عدد) در سبد خرید قرار دارد`, 'warning'); and `حداکثر تعداد مجاز ${MAX_CART_QUANTITY} عدد می‌باشد` — MAX_CART_QUANTITY (constants.ts:13 = 99) is interpolated raw, unlike the rest of the UI which uses toPersianDigits.
finding.suggested_fix: Wrap with toPersianDigits(MAX_CART_QUANTITY) — import from lib/utils like other components.

finding.title: Coupon validation response leaks internal usage data via raw row
finding.suggested_fix: `coupon` is the raw DB row including usedCount/usageLimit/expiresAt internals. Return only {code,label,percent,amount,minTotal} plus computed discount/finalTotal.

finding.title: CSP scriptSrc includes 'unsafe-inline' and imgSrc allows plain http:
finding.suggested_fix: Replace 'unsafe-inline' with nonce- or hash-based script policy (Vite bundles are external files; inline usage is small). Drop `http:` from imgSrc to avoid mixed-content loading of attacker-influenced product image URLs. Weakens XSS containment if an injection ever lands.

finding.title: PUT /api/admin/users/:id/role returns the full DB row including the bcrypt password hash
finding.suggested_fix: Destructure out `password` before responding (`const { password, ...safe } = updated`), matching the pattern used in GET /users (line 275-278). Admin-only, but the hash then sits in browser devtools/proxies/logs unnecessarily.
